tasks.short: Select digital images, enter print quantities and release the checked print job.

steps.what: Retrieve digital image files and the customer's print requirements
Select digital images for printing and resolve image suitability questions
Specify print quantities, sizes, media and image layout in the print job
Check the image selection, copies, crop, colour profile and printer destination
Check the final print job version and direct it to the printer

tasks.design: Configure job views and batch print presets in {OTHER}, the photo printing application, using the job reference from {OPS_SYSTEM}. Image choice remains human, and print configuration, checking and actual printer release are separate steps.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated job navigation and per-image print settings add handling.
tasks.enabler_now: Native batch settings and print presets can reuse common quantity, media and layout fields.
tasks.still_hard: Correct image choice, crop and colour appearance for the customer's request.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can spot an unsuitable image or unintended crop.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repetitive print configuration while preserving output choice and release control.

reach.learn: Check presets against actual customer requirements

evidence.claim: Native batch print presets and job views can reduce repeated settings; no measured photographic-processing result is supplied.

assumptions: Includes image selection, quantity and setting entry and real printer release; no customer delivery or upload is implied.
Operator produces file selection, copy count, size, media, crop and printer choice in s2-s3, with capture time counted. Missing or conflicting order details require manual clarification.
OTHER means existing photo printing software; native batch settings first, no AI image selection.
s5 is the real job release and stays fully retained; ordinary configuration saving earns no separate saving or approval.
unknowns: Existing batch preset use and consistency of customer print instructions
research_questions: How much setting entry repeats across images in the same job?

incremental.description: Maintain print presets and test changed media profiles

approvals.approved_version: Exact file list, copy counts, crops, colour/media settings and target printer; any changed job requires a fresh release check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=88, gross=12, upkeep=2, central net=10 E1. Low: mixed output sizes and per-image crops defeat batch presets, retaining 98 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: consistent media and quantities allow some batch settings while image suitability and crop checks stay manual, retaining 92 hours plus upkeep for 6 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and scan photographic originals, check digitisation quality and save the files.

steps.what: Inspect, clean and position negatives, prints or other images for scanning
Determine resolution, colour mode, bit depth and output requirements
Configure scanner settings and image naming for the selected specification
Operate scanners and handle originals through the digitisation sequence
Check focus, completeness, colour and defects against the photographic originals
Save the checked digitised image files in the existing job location

tasks.design: Configure reusable scan presets in {OTHER}, the scanner application. Physical preparation, scanner operation and image-quality checks remain human; only repeated setting entry is reduced, and the ordinary same-system save stays fully retained.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated scan-setting entry adds a small clerical component to physical digitisation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native scan presets can reuse settings for comparable originals.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile media, focus, dust and source-specific colour or exposure problems.
tasks.human_edge: The operator can handle the original safely and compare the scan with it.
tasks.altitude: Reduce repeated settings around hands-on scanning.

reach.learn: Select presets according to actual source condition

evidence.claim: Native scanner presets can reduce repeated configuration; no measured labour saving is supplied.

assumptions: Counts active labour rather than unattended scan duration; no new scanner hardware or automated original handling is assumed.
Operator produces resolution, colour mode, bit depth, output format and naming fields in s2-s3, with capture counted. Unsuitable presets or unusual originals require manual settings.
OTHER means existing scanner software; native presets first, no AI quality acceptance.
Ordinary save s6 remains one percent fully retained and has no self-approval.
unknowns: Preset availability and proportion of comparable originals
research_questions: How much active configuration time remains after existing presets?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=97, gross=3, upkeep=1, central net=2 E1. Low: mixed film formats and source damage require bespoke scan settings, retaining 99 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: some comparable prints fit presets but source-specific settings remain, retaining 98 hours plus upkeep for 1 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Connect image sources, configure a local import and verify copied image files.

steps.what: Connect cameras, flash memory cards or USB devices and identify the source media
Select image files, job destination and import naming settings
Load digital images onto the computer using the existing local copy function
Verify image counts, file readability and destination against the source
Record the imported source, image count, job reference and file location
Save the import record in the existing job

tasks.design: Configure native import naming and destination presets in {OTHER}, the image import application, with job record fields in {OPS_SYSTEM}. Connecting media, the existing copy operation and verification stay retained; only repeated setup and record entry are reduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Import setup and job documentation repeat source and destination fields.
tasks.enabler_now: Native import presets and record defaults can reuse an explicit job reference.
tasks.still_hard: Damaged files, wrong media and correct job ownership.
tasks.human_edge: The operator verifies that the expected images actually arrived intact.
tasks.altitude: Reduce import administration while retaining source and copy verification.

reach.learn: Check source identity and destination integrity

evidence.claim: Native import presets and job record defaults can reduce repeated setup; existing digital copying itself earns no new saving.

assumptions: Includes media connection, selection, actual local copy, verification and existing import record; no external upload, deletion or source overwrite.

Operator produces source identity, selected file set, destination and naming fields in s1-s2 and actual count/location in s5, with capture counted. Unreadable sources or ambiguous job identity require manual handling.
OTHER means existing local image import software; native presets first, no custom file-copy integration.
s3 counts existing active copy handling, not unattended transfer time, and retains it fully. Ordinary local copies and same-system record saves introduce no self-approval or claimed transfer saving.
unknowns: Existing import presets and job record practice
research_questions: How much import handling repeats destination and naming choices?

already_counted.description: Capture source and import record details

incremental.description: Maintain import presets and job defaults

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=93.3, gross=6.7, upkeep=2, central net=4.7 E1. Low: mixed devices and inconsistent job metadata force manual setup and records, retaining 98 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: compatible naming and job references allow partial reuse while connection and verification remain full, retaining 95 hours plus upkeep for 3 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and operate specialist photographic transfer or enlargement equipment and check the output.

steps.what: Retrieve the film transfer or photographic enlargement requirements
Inspect source film or images and determine suitable processing settings
Set up special equipment for the chosen transfer or enlargement
Operate special equipment to transfer film or produce photographic enlargements
Check transfer continuity or enlargement focus, exposure, colour and completeness
Record the processing settings, output identity and quality findings

tasks.design: Use native job views in {OPS_SYSTEM} and reusable settings where supported by {OTHER}, the specialist transfer or enlargement equipment controls. Source assessment, physical setup and operation remain human, with the processing record separately priced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated job lookup, supported setting entry and record fields add small clerical overhead.
tasks.enabler_now: Native presets can reuse a limited subset of settings for comparable source media.
tasks.still_hard: Legacy media, physical setup and judging image quality.
tasks.human_edge: The operator adapts to the original's condition and checks the actual result.
tasks.altitude: Reduce small repetitive setup and record portions around specialist operation.

reach.learn: Document settings and source-specific quality limits

evidence.claim: Where existing specialist controls support presets, some repeated settings and record fields may be reused; no measured photographic transfer benefit is supplied.

assumptions: Includes actual operation, its record and current output checks; no hardware replacement or automated media handling.

Operator produces output format or enlargement size, source identity and settings in s2-s3 and output quality findings in s5-s6, with capture counted. Unsupported controls or unusual media require full manual setup.
OTHER means existing transfer or enlargement controls; native presets first, and the estimate does not apply to equipment lacking reusable settings.
Ordinary processing record saves remain retained without self-approval; no external delivery is implied.
unknowns: Equipment preset support and source media comparability
research_questions: Which active setup settings are repeated and supported by native presets?

already_counted.description: Capture processing settings and quality findings

incremental.description: Maintain supported presets and record fields

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=95, gross=5, upkeep=1, central net=4 E1. Low: legacy analogue controls and unusual source condition prevent preset reuse, retaining 99 hours plus upkeep for zero net. High: compatible equipment presets reduce limited setting entry while physical alignment and quality checks stay full, retaining 97 hours plus upkeep for 2 net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain visual judgement and physical photographic handling while reducing repeated settings and records.
reach: Coordinate clear job and source identities with printing and archive colleagues
role.ambitious_version: A photographic operator who spends less time re-entering settings and more time protecting originals and output quality.
